entries.title: How can saving a little at a time help you reach a goal?
entries.answer: Saving means setting aside money you can use later. Imagine a model kit costs fifteen dollars and you have five now. If you add two dollars at a time, you need five more additions to reach your goal. Keeping track shows how close you are and helps you decide whether to spend some of the money on something else. People can also save for a need that they cannot plan for in advance.
facts: A clear target and a way to track progress can make a savings plan easier to follow.

entries.title: How can supply and demand affect a price?
entries.answer: Supply has to do with how much sellers are willing to offer at different prices. Demand has to do with how much buyers are willing and able to buy at different prices. Imagine a market where one stall has five baskets of berries and lots of shoppers want them. The berries might sell at a higher price than they would when many stalls have lots of berries for sale. Other things such as the cost of growing and bringing berries to market can matter too.
facts: A shortage means buyers want more of a thing than sellers are offering at the current price.

entries.title: How does a budget help you plan?
entries.answer: A budget is a plan for using money. Imagine you expect to have twelve dollars this month. You might plan to use five for a craft, save four, and leave three for a later choice. If the plan calls for spending more than you have, you can look for something to change or wait for more money. A household can use the same idea to plan for regular bills and things that come up from time to time.
facts: A budget can include money to save as well as money you plan to spend right away.

entries.title: How does barter work?
entries.answer: Barter means trading something directly for something else. You might trade a comic you have already read for a book a friend has finished. The two of you would each have something the other wants. But what if your friend has the book and wants a pencil instead? You would have to find a pencil or work out another trade. That is one reason people find it easier to trade many different things when everyone uses the same kind of money.
facts: People can offer to do a job as part of a barter trade.
A barter offer only works when everyone involved accepts the exchange.

entries.title: How does borrowing money work?
entries.answer: A loan is money someone lends you under an agreement that you will pay it back. Imagine borrowing five dollars to buy art paper, knowing you can return the five next week. Some loans also charge interest, which is extra money for getting to use the borrowed money now. A loan agreement says when payments are due and how much they will be. The money gives you a choice today and a payment to make later.
facts: The amount you borrow at the start is called the principal.

entries.title: What do you give up when you choose one thing?
entries.answer: If you have enough tickets for either one ride or a snack, choosing the ride means giving up the snack. The snack is your opportunity cost if it was the next choice you would have made. An opportunity cost can involve time too. Spending your one free hour on a game could mean missing a chance to finish a drawing. Thinking about the next best choice can help you decide what matters more to you.
facts: Your opportunity cost is the next best choice you give up.

entries.title: What does a bank do with an account?
entries.answer: A bank account is a record of money a bank is holding for a person or group. Putting money into the account is called a deposit. Taking money out is a withdrawal. Some accounts help people pay for everyday purchases, and others are meant to hold money people want to save. The amount shown after money moves in and out is the balance. Banks also lend money, which borrowers agree to pay back.
facts: People can put money in or take it out without needing to use the exact same paper bills each time.

entries.title: What does inflation do to what money can buy?
entries.answer: Inflation means prices for many ordinary goods and services are rising overall. If the price of a pack of crayons goes up while most other prices stay the same, that one change alone tells us little about inflation. People who measure it look at prices for a wide group of things. When those prices rise overall, the same amount of money usually buys less than it did before, even if some prices fall.
facts: People who measure inflation compare a group of prices at different times.

entries.title: What does scarcity have to do with making choices?
entries.answer: Scarcity means that the resources available cannot cover every use people want for them. Think of a class with enough paper for one large banner or for several paper airplanes. Using the paper for the banner leaves less for airplanes. Time can be scarce too. There may be time for one game before lunch, even when the class has lots of games. Scarcity means people have to choose what to do first or what to leave out.
facts: Something can be scarce even if there is a fair amount of it, because people want to use more than they have.

entries.title: What is a euro?
entries.answer: The euro is a kind of money used in many European countries, including France. A euro is divided into 100 cents. If you travel between countries that use the euro, you can compare prices and spend euro coins in either place. Take a close look at a euro coin. One side has a design used in common, while the other side can have a design chosen by the country that issued the coin. Different designs can still have the same value.
facts: Each euro is worth 100 euro cents.
The symbol for the euro is €.

entries.title: What is the difference between an import and an export?
entries.answer: When people sell something from one country to someone in another, the sale is an export for the country it comes from. It is an import for the country that buys it. Imagine a store in one country buys pots from a maker abroad. The pots are imports at the store and exports where they were made. Trade can also involve services, such as hiring a person in another country to help design a book.
facts: The same thing can be called an import or an export depending on whose side of the sale you are looking at.

entries.title: What is the difference between goods and services?
entries.answer: Goods are things people use, buy, or trade, such as a pencil, a loaf of bread, or a bicycle. A service is work someone does for others, such as cutting hair, fixing a bike, or driving a bus. One trip to a store can include both: a baker might sell you a cake and charge a separate amount to have it delivered. The cake is a good, and delivering it is a service.
facts: One person or business can provide goods, services, or both.

entries.title: Who are producers and consumers?
entries.answer: A producer makes a good or supplies a service. A person who uses a good or service is a consumer. A grower who sells apples is a producer, and someone who eats an apple is a consumer. The same person can be both at different times. A baker makes bread for customers and may ride a bus to work. At the bakery the baker is producing bread, and on the bus the baker is using a ride.
facts: A business can buy goods or services to help make something else.

entries.title: Why can interest make an amount of money grow?
entries.answer: Interest is extra money paid for using someone else’s money. A bank may pay you interest to hold money in a savings account. If you borrow money, you may pay interest to the lender. For example, in a simple made-up loan, a borrower receives ten dollars and pays back eleven. The extra dollar is interest. How much interest is paid depends on the agreement, the amount of money, and how long someone uses the money.
facts: Interest can add to savings or increase what a borrower has to pay back.

entries.title: Why do people divide up the work of making something?
entries.answer: Imagine making costumes for a class play. One person measures the cloth, one cuts out the shapes, and another stitches them together. If each person practices one job, they can often do it well and do more of it. This way of focusing on part of the work is called specialization. It can help groups make more things together. The group still needs each person’s work, so the steps have to fit one another.
facts: Specialization can happen between people, businesses, or places that focus on different kinds of work.

entries.title: Why do people use money?
entries.answer: Money makes it easier to buy and sell things. Imagine you make a hat and want a book. If the person with the book does not want a hat, you can sell your hat to someone else and use the money for the book. A common money unit also gives people a way to compare costs. A book priced at ten dollars costs twice as much as one priced at five dollars. People can also save money and use it for something later.
facts: Coins and paper bills are examples of money people can hold.
Merchants can list prices in a shared money unit such as dollars.
